canonical_changes.before: Distinct proposed versions: House H.5175 chapter 164 section 163 defines data centers by designed load of at least 20 MW and digital-data purpose; specified new/expanded permit applicants face at least 80% renewable supply and a battery-infeasibility showing before fossil-backup permitting, alongside data-center tariffs protecting other customers. Senate S.3166 section 3 proposes data-center exemption certification conditions; sections 88 and 114 propose flexible interconnection and a working group including data-center operators. Version differences remain explicit; these are not enacted requirements.
canonical_changes.after: Distinct proposed versions: House H.5175 proposes chapter 164 section 163, defining a data center by a designed load of at least 20 MW and digital-data purpose. Specified new or expanded data centers seeking permits from the department or the energy facilities siting board would procure sufficient electricity for operational needs using at least 80% renewable resources; those seeking a Department of Environmental Protection permit to operate fossil-fuel backup generation would first demonstrate on-site battery storage infeasibility. The House also proposes data-center tariffs protecting other ratepayers and incentivizing efficiency. Senate S.3166 section 3 proposes conditions for specified data-center tax benefits; sections 88 and 114 propose flexible interconnection and a working group including data-center representatives. The excerpts do not establish enactment of either version or the provisions' present force.
